analysis:
Examined LaunchAgent.swift (head) and the EngineV2ProductionWiringTests.swift patch and base excerpt.

LaunchAgent.swift (lines 284-286, 296-297): two new env keys, ToolStreamPreparation.streamToolCallsEnvironmentKey and ReasoningPromptProbe.plainTailContentSeedEnvironmentKey, are added to inferencePassthroughEnvKeys. They flow through passthroughEnvironment (lines 327-348), which forwards only non-empty allowlisted values into the launchd plist EnvironmentVariables. The doc comment describes both as behavior toggles with exact 0 as the rollback. These are inference-behavior toggles for streamed tool calls and a Qwen content seed. They are not secrets, credentials, trust-policy or authorization inputs, and they sit apart from the App Attest worker opt-in handling (lines 335-339), which is unchanged. The plist is written to the user's own LaunchAgents directory, so the operator already controls it (ADV-001 is already in scope under TB-003). The change adds no new privilege or trust boundary crossing. Stop/disable, drain and watchdog semantics are unchanged.

Tests (EngineV2ProductionWiringTests.swift, lines 312 and 1308-1389): the test helper now handles the new .toolCallDelta event case, and new tests parametrize the model type for plain-tail Qwen handling. These are test-only changes with no production security effect.

Limits: the production implementations of ToolStreamPreparation, ReasoningPromptProbe and the .toolCallDelta streaming path are not in the supplied evidence. I could not check whether incremental tool-call deltas stay inside the existing E2E encryption and fail-closed path (T-008), or whether tool-call argument deltas are validated or bounded. The next pass should review those files if they are in the PR. The relevant context is the TB-002 response encryption path and T-008 for plaintext streaming on encryption failure. There is no evidence of a regression in the supplied units. The default-on streaming behavior is a change to confirm in the unseen sources.
